page_title: Want an unfair advantage in your tech career? Consume content meant for other roles

sources.entry: Want an unfair advantage in your tech career? Consume content meant for other roles

summary.title: Want an unfair advantage in your tech career? Consume content meant for other roles
summary.one_liner: Reading and watching content written for other tech roles (recruiters, product, managers) builds empathy, avoids inter-role misunderstandings, and gives you a career edge.
takeaways: Seeking out content made for other roles (recruiters, product, CEOs, QA, sales) gives a perspective that coffee chats often miss.
Understanding other roles builds empathy and helps you avoid assuming colleagues do little work.
Knowing what other roles value (e.g., recruiters' use of Boolean search and company filters) lets you act strategically with them.
Engineering leaders benefit from cross-functional understanding, and switching between IC and management roles deepens it.
The post lists suggested resources per role, such as Reforge for product and Ben Horowitz's book for CEOs.
summary.summary: The author argues that tech professionals gain a competitive advantage by consuming content (podcasts, talks, newsletters, courses) created for roles they work with, rather than only their own. He explains benefits: content is available anytime, people speak more candidly to insiders, and it builds empathy and helps avoid common friction between roles like recruiters and hiring managers. He illustrates with a recruiter talk on advanced LinkedIn Boolean search and closes with a list of suggested resources for product, CEO, recruiting, director/VP, and staff engineer roles.
